HU110: Budapest was formed in 1873 by uniting three cities: Buda, Óbuda, and Pest. Its Chain Bridge was among Europe's first permanent suspension bridges.
HU231: Baranya is home to Pécs, one of Europe's oldest university cities — the University of Pécs was founded in 1367, the first university in Hungary.
HU331: Bács-Kiskun's sandy soil produces exceptional apricots used in Hungary's famous Barack pálinka brandy — the county lies at the heart of the Great Hungarian Plain.
HU332: Békés county sits on some of the richest agricultural land in Hungary and it is also the birthplace of the famous csabai and gyulai sausages as well.
HU311: This county contains the Aggtelek karst cave system, a UNESCO World Heritage Site with over 700 caves, including the vast Baradla Cave.
HU333: Csongrád-Csanád is home to Szeged, the paprika capital of Hungary — its red paprika holds a protected geographical indication and is used in goulash worldwide.
HU211: Fejér county contains Székesfehérvár, Hungary's ancient coronation city, where 37 kings and queens were crowned and 15 are buried.
HU221: This county contains Sopron, which voted in 1921 to remain part of Hungary rather than join Austria — earning it the enduring title "Most Loyal City."
HU321: Hajdú-Bihar is home to Debrecen, Hungary's second-largest city, and the Great Forest (Nagyerdő) — Hungary's only national park within a city.
HU312: Heves county is home to the Eger wine region, famous for the legendary red blend Egri Bikavér — "Bull's Blood of Eger."
HU322: This county sits at the confluence of the Tisza and Körös rivers and is a historic centre of Hungary's fishing tradition and paprika cultivation.
HU212: Komárom-Esztergom is home to Esztergom, Hungary's first capital and the seat of the Archbishop — its basilica is the largest church in Hungary.
HU313: Nógrád is Hungary's least populated county and contains Hollókő, a UNESCO World Heritage Village that preserves traditional Palóc folk architecture.
HU120: Pest county completely surrounds Budapest and contains Visegrád, the royal castle where medieval Hungarian kings held their royal court during the 14th and 15th centuries.
HU232: Somogy county stretches along Lake Balaton's southern shore — the lake is the largest freshwater lake in Central Europe, covering 592 sq km.
HU323: This county borders both Ukraine and Romania and is known for its apple orchards — it produces more apples than any other county in Hungary.
HU233: Tolna county lies along the Danube and is known for the Sárköz region, one of Hungary's richest ethnographic areas, celebrated for its embroidery and folk traditions.
HU222: Vas county borders Austria and Slovenia and contains Kőszeg, whose small garrison famously held off the Ottoman army for 25 days in 1532.
HU213: Veszprém is known as the "City of Queens" — it was the traditional residence of Hungarian queens and home to one of Hungary's oldest episcopal seats.
HU223: Zala county is home to Lake Hévíz, the world's largest biologically active natural thermal lake, which stays above 23°C even in winter.
